1.outline: Term theme: 'Text Coding: Python'. Compare a block program with the same logic written as Python text in Thonny.
objectives: Compare a block program with its Python text equivalent.
Open and run a simple program in Thonny.
Identify print() as the block equivalent of 'say' or 'show'.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Same idea, new form
plan.detail: Show a simple block program next to its Python text equivalent — same logic, different look.

plan.title: First Thonny run
plan.detail: Open Thonny, type print("Hello"), run it, and change the message.

plan.title: Spot the pattern
plan.detail: Match three more block-to-text pairs on the comparison sheet. Log out.

successCriteria: I can compare a block and its Python equivalent.
I ran a working Python program in Thonny.
I can match blocks to their Python text form.

2.outline: Learn input() to ask the user a question and print() to respond, building a simple 'ask and answer' program.
objectives: Use input() to ask a question.
Store the answer in a variable.
Use print() to respond using that variable.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Ask and respond
plan.detail: Demo name = input("What's your name? ") then print("Hello " + name).

plan.title: Build one
plan.detail: Write a program that asks two questions and responds using both answers.

plan.title: Test it
plan.detail: Test with a partner's real answers. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I used input() to ask a question.
I stored the answer in a variable.
I used print() to respond using that variable.

3.outline: Learn the difference between text (str) and numbers (int), and use int() to convert typed input into a number for maths.
objectives: Explain the difference between text and number data.
Use int() to convert input into a number.
Perform a calculation using converted input.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Text vs numbers
plan.detail: Show input() always returns text — try to add two typed numbers and watch it fail or concatenate oddly.

plan.title: int(input())
plan.detail: Fix it with int(input(...)), then build a program that adds two numbers the user types in.

plan.title: Test edge cases
plan.detail: Test with 0, a negative number, and a large number. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I can explain why input() needs int() for maths.
I built a working number-adding program.
I tested my program with edge-case values.

4.outline: Move from the desktop to the micro:bit, writing simple Python that runs on the physical device.
4.sowResources: MakeCode (Python view) or Mu editor, micro:bit devices.
objectives: Write a simple Python program for the micro:bit.
Flash it onto a physical device.
Compare it with the equivalent desktop Python.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: micro:bit Python setup
plan.detail: Open the Python editor for micro:bit and look at a simple starter program.

plan.title: Write and flash
plan.detail: Write a short program (e.g. show a scrolling message) and flash it onto the device.

plan.title: Compare
plan.detail: Compare the micro:bit code with the desktop version from earlier weeks. Log out.

successCriteria: I wrote a working Python program for the micro:bit.
I flashed it onto a physical device successfully.
I can compare it with the desktop version.

5.outline: Practise reading a Python error message to find the line and the fault, then fix it.
objectives: Read a Python traceback to find the error line.
Identify common error types: NameError, SyntaxError.
Fix a broken program using the error message.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Reading a traceback
plan.detail: Show a traceback and point out the line number and error type.

plan.title: Fix three bugs
plan.detail: Work through three short broken programs, reading each error before fixing it.

plan.title: Share a fix
plan.detail: Share the trickiest bug found and how the error message helped. Log out.

successCriteria: I can find the line number from an error message.
I can name at least one common error type.
I fixed at least two of the three broken programs.

6.outline: Build a small useful program — a simple calculator or a unit converter — using input, variables and maths.
objectives: Plan a small useful program.
Build it using input, variables and calculations.
Test it with sensible values.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Choose a project
plan.detail: Choose calculator or converter (e.g. cm to inches).

plan.title: Build it
plan.detail: Write the program using input(), int()/float() and a calculation.

plan.title: Test it
plan.detail: Test with two or three sensible values. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I chose and planned a small program.
My program takes input and calculates a result.
I tested it with sensible values.

7.outline: Test the program with edge cases (zero, negative, very large numbers) and improve it based on what breaks.
objectives: Test a program with edge-case values.
Identify what breaks or behaves oddly.
Improve the program to handle it better.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What is an edge case?
plan.detail: Recap edge cases from earlier weeks: zero, negative, very large or very small.

plan.title: Test and fix
plan.detail: Test the calculator/converter with edge cases and fix anything that breaks or looks wrong.

plan.title: Peer test
plan.detail: Swap with a partner and try to break each other's program. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I tested my program with at least two edge cases.
I fixed at least one issue found.
A partner tested my program and it held up.

8.outline: Demo the finished program to the class, explaining what it does and how the code works.
objectives: Demo a working program to the class.
Explain how the program works in simple terms.
Answer one question about the code.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Showcase demos
plan.detail: Each pupil demos their program briefly, running it live.

plan.title: Code explanation
plan.detail: Explain one part of the code to a partner or the class.

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: Save the .py file to the portfolio folder. Log out.

successCriteria: I demoed my working program.
I explained how part of my code works.
My .py file is saved to the portfolio folder.

9.outline: Add one useful improvement to the program — input validation, a friendlier message, or an extra calculation.
objectives: Choose one useful improvement.
Implement it without breaking existing features.
Re-test after the change.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Add a feature
plan.detail: Add validation, a friendlier message, or an extra calculation to the program.

plan.title: Re-test
plan.detail: Re-run the program to check the original features still work.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: I added one useful improvement.
The original features still work.
My improved program is saved.

10.outline: Rehearse the term's Python skills in pairs: input, variables, calculation, debugging.
10.sowResources: Recap slide deck, practice task cards.
objectives: Recall the term's Python skills in order.
Rehearse writing and testing a small program with a partner.
Identify the trickiest step.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Skill recap
plan.detail: Recap: input, convert, calculate, debug — as a class chant.

plan.title: Paired rehearsal
plan.detail: Write and test a small program with a partner reading the task card, then swap.

plan.title: Tricky step check
plan.detail: Name the step you still find hardest. Log out.

successCriteria: I can list the term's Python skills in order.
I rehearsed writing a program with a partner.
I know which step needs more practice.

11.outline: Individual task: write a Python program that takes input, uses variables, and produces output — on screen and, if time allows, on a micro:bit.
objectives: Translate a given brief into working Python code.
Use input, output and variables correctly.
Debug a text-code error if one appears.

plan.title: Settle and explain
plan.detail: Calm start — explain the task and rubric.

plan.title: Build the program
plan.detail: Individual practical: write a program to the given brief using input/output/variables.

plan.title: Test and fix
plan.detail: Test the program and fix any errors found.

plan.title: Celebrate
plan.detail: Save and celebrate the term's progress. Log out.

successCriteria: My program takes input and produces output.
I used variables and data types correctly.
I read an error message and fixed it if needed.
